literal: He was transferred to be commander of the Tujing garrison and strove to discipline himself deeply.
idiomatic: He was made commander of the Tujing garrison and applied himself with strict self-discipline.

literal: Later the Tujing garrison was changed to Fenzhou, and Pi was still appointed inspector.
idiomatic: When the Tujing garrison was reorganized as Fenzhou, Pi remained its governor.

literal: The former Tujing prefect Liu Sheng had great authority and kindness in the commandery; when his term ended and he returned to the capital, more than eight hundred Hu came to Pi to request him.
idiomatic: Former prefect Liu Sheng had ruled Tujing with authority and kindness; when his term ended and he returned to court, over eight hundred Hu petitioned Pi to bring him back.

literal: The former Dingyang magistrate Wu Pingren also had grace and trust; households increased severalfold.
idiomatic: Former Dingyang magistrate Wu Pingren likewise won trust, and registered households multiplied several times over.

literal: Because officials and people cherished them, Pi memorialized to request both; Emperor Xiaowen approved all.
idiomatic: Pi, seeing how officials and commoners cherished them, memorialized for both appointments, and Emperor Xiaowen granted each request.

literal: Since Pi had repeatedly recommended Sheng and the rest, the prefects and magistrates under his jurisdiction all sharpened themselves; awe and transformation spread widely.
idiomatic: Pi's repeated recommendations of Sheng and others spurred every prefect and magistrate under him to sharpen their conduct, and his moral authority transformed the region.

literal: More than seven hundred men of the province, Li Gui and Guo Jizu among them, went to the palace gates to praise Pi's kindness and virtue.
idiomatic: Over seven hundred provincials, including Li Gui and Guo Jizu, went to the capital to praise Pi's kindness and virtue.

literal: Emperor Xiaowen, because Pi's governance was sound and the people pleased, raised his rank and extended his term.
idiomatic: Seeing sound governance and a content populace, Emperor Xiaowen raised Pi's rank and extended his term of office.

literal: Later he was summoned as Director of the Imperial Household; according to precedent his princely title was reduced to Duke of Weijun.
idiomatic: He was later summoned to be Director of the Imperial Household and, by precedent, reduced from prince to Duke of Weijun.

literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary and Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat.
idiomatic: He rose through Attendant-in-Ordinary to Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat.

literal: In Mu Tai's rebellion Pi had secretly communicated with him; after an amnesty the matter came out, and his enfeoffment was stripped—he became a registered commoner.
idiomatic: During Mu Tai's rebellion Pi had secretly communicated with the plotters; after an amnesty exposed the affair, his fief was revoked and he was reduced to common registration.

literal: He died at home.
idiomatic: He died at home.

literal: Under Emperor Xuanwu he was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Hengzhou.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Xuanwu he was posthumously made General Who Pacifies the North and Inspector of Hengzhou.

literal: Pi's younger brother Liang, courtesy name Youfu, early showed bearing and style.
idiomatic: Pi's younger brother Liang, courtesy name Youfu, showed refinement and presence from youth.

literal: Under Emperor Xianwen he first entered service as Attendant Censor.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Xianwen he began his career as Attendant Censor.

literal: He married the Princess of Zhongshan, was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards, and enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao.
idiomatic: He married the Princess of Zhongshan, was made Commandant of the Horse Guards, and enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao.

literal: He was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and his fief was changed to Prince of Changle.
idiomatic: He was made Attendant-in-Ordinary and transferred to the princedom of Changle.

literal: Under Emperor Xiaowen he was appointed General Who Pacifies the South, Colonel Protector of the Western Rong, and garrison commander of Chouchi.
idiomatic: Under Emperor Xiaowen he was made General Who Pacifies the South, Colonel Protector of the Western Rong, and commander of the Chouchi garrison.

literal: The King of Dangchang, Liang Miji, died; his son Mibo succeeded.
idiomatic: Dangchang king Liang Miji died, and his son Mibo succeeded.

literal: Pressed by Tuyuhun, he came to flee to Chouchi.
idiomatic: Harried by Tuyuhun, Mibo fled to Chouchi for refuge.

literal: Liang considered Mibo violent and perverse, abandoned by the Di and Qiang;
idiomatic: Liang judged Mibo violent and perverse and abandoned by the Di and Qiang tribes;

literal: Miji's elder brother's son Micheng, whom the tribesmen gladly followed, memorialized asking to receive him.
idiomatic: Miji's nephew Micheng, whom the tribes gladly followed, memorialized asking that he be installed instead.

literal: Emperor Xiaowen approved.
idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen agreed.

literal: Thereupon he routed Tuyuhun, installed Micheng, and returned.
idiomatic: He then drove off Tuyuhun, installed Micheng, and withdrew.

literal: The Di chieftain Yang Bu, since Yanxing, had followed the army through twenty-one battles; former garrison commanders had suppressed him and never reported his merit.
idiomatic: The Di chieftain Yang Bu had fought in twenty-one campaigns since Yanxing, yet successive garrison commanders had suppressed his record and never reported his merit.

literal: Liang memorialized to make Bu Grand Warden of Guangye; the powerful families were all pleased, and within the borders there was great peace.
idiomatic: Liang memorialized to appoint Bu Grand Warden of Guangye; local magnates were pleased and the region knew great peace.

literal: He was summoned as Attendant-in-Ordinary and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
idiomatic: He was summoned to be Attendant-in-Ordinary and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.

literal: At that time Sizhou was re-established.
idiomatic: At that time Sizhou was re-established.

literal: Emperor Xiaowen said: "Sizhou has just been founded and has no staff officers; a Rectifier must be appointed to fix selections.
idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowen said, "Sizhou has only just been founded and lacks staff; we must appoint a Rectifier to govern selection."

literal: Yet the Rectifier's post requires both virtue and renown.
idiomatic: "That office demands both virtue and public standing."

literal: Under Emperor Shizu, Cui Hao was Rectifier of Jizhou and Changsun Song Rectifier of Sizhou—truly men well chosen.
idiomatic: "Under Emperor Shizu, Cui Hao was Rectifier of Jizhou and Changsun Song Rectifier of Sizhou—true examples of the right choice."

literal: You ministers and grandees should deliberate and recommend carefully.
idiomatic: "You ministers should deliberate and recommend with care."

literal: Director of the Masters of Writing Lu Rui recommended Liang as Grand Rectifier of Sizhou.
idiomatic: Director Lu Rui recommended Liang as Grand Rectifier of Sizhou.

literal: Later he was appointed Minister of Works and took part in deliberating the code of laws.
idiomatic: He was later made Minister of Works and helped draft the code of laws.

literal: By precedent his noble rank was reduced to duke.
idiomatic: By precedent his title was reduced to duke.

literal: When the Empress Dowager Wenming had died, more than a month had passed, yet Emperor Xiaowen was still emaciated from grief.
idiomatic: Though more than a month had passed since Empress Dowager Wenming's death, Emperor Xiaowen remained wasted with grief.

literal: Liang memorialized asking that above he uphold the golden-book testament, below he voice the heart of the hundred millions.
idiomatic: Liang memorialized that the emperor should above honor the golden-book testament and below speak for the hearts of the realm.

literal: At the time he wore light mourning garb and repeatedly took ordinary meals;
idiomatic: The emperor then wore light mourning, took ordinary meals again,

literal: restored suburban sacrifices, and extended grace in full measure.
idiomatic: restored suburban sacrifices, and extended grace throughout the ranks.

literal: An edict said: "If filial piety and brotherly duty reach their utmost, nothing is blocked.
idiomatic: An edict said, "When filial piety and brotherly duty reach their utmost, nothing remains blocked."

literal: Now fierce winds and great drought persist and timely rain does not fall—truly because sincere longing is not yet deep and the hidden and manifest are unmoved.
idiomatic: "Yet fierce winds and drought persist while timely rain withholds itself—because your longing is not yet deep enough for hidden and manifest alike to respond."

literal: Soon after he also held Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
idiomatic: He soon also became Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

literal: When the Taiji Hall was to be built, the emperor received the ministers at Taihua Hall and said: "We are about to raise palace halls and now wish to move to Yongle to escape dust and clamor.
idiomatic: When the Taiji Hall was to be built, the emperor received the ministers at Taihua Hall and said, "We are about to raise new halls and will move to Yongle to escape dust and noise."

literal: Though in timber and earth I am again without heart, can destroying them fail to wring grief!
idiomatic: "Though I am no builder at heart, how can tearing them down fail to wring my heart!"

literal: Now I therefore face you and take leave together.
idiomatic: "I have called you here to take leave together."

literal: This hall was made by Emperor Gaozong, passed through Emperor Xianzu, and in my tender years I received the throne here.
idiomatic: "This hall was built by Emperor Gaozong, passed through Emperor Xianzu, and in my tender years I received the throne here."

literal: But affairs seize feeling; there will be a change in design.
idiomatic: "But necessity overrides sentiment, and the design must change."

literal: Looking up to days past, I am only deeply grieved.
idiomatic: "Looking back on those days fills me only with grief."

literal: Liang bowed his head and asked to consult divination by tortoise and milfoil.
idiomatic: Liang bowed and asked to consult the oracle by tortoise and milfoil.

literal: He also said that last year's labor projects had accomplished very much—the Imperial Ancestral Temple and Bright Hall were finished within a year.
idiomatic: He added that last year's labor had already accomplished much—the Imperial Ancestral Temple and Bright Hall had been finished within a year.

literal: If works are raised year after year, I fear human strength will be carved to exhaustion.
idiomatic: "If works are raised year after year, I fear the people will be exhausted."

literal: Moreover timber has just been freshly cut; I wish to wait further years.
idiomatic: "Fresh timber has only just been cut; let it season a few more years."

literal: The emperor said: "I have looked far back at former kings—none failed to build.
idiomatic: The emperor said, "I have looked far back at former kings, and none failed to build."

literal: Therefore when Zhou founded its enterprise it raised the Spirit Terrace;
idiomatic: "When Zhou founded its enterprise it raised the Spirit Terrace;"

literal: when mighty Han received the Mandate, Weiyang was made.
idiomatic: "when mighty Han received the Mandate, Weiyang was built."

literal: At the very founding they were still like this;
idiomatic: "Even at founding they did as much;"

literal: how much more I, who inherit the fortune of many sages and stand on a foundation of great peace, wishing to seize this time to complete the great work!
idiomatic: "how much more should I, inheriting many sages' fortune upon an age of great peace, seize this moment to finish the great work!"

literal: Man's allotted portion fixes short and long life;
idiomatic: "A man's allotted span fixes short life or long;"

literal: though milfoil and tortoise may be wise, what can they do against fate!
idiomatic: "milfoil and tortoise may be wise, but what can they do against fate!"

literal: What is entrusted to one's portion—how could it depend on divination!
idiomatic: "What fate entrusts does not wait on divination!"

literal: He moved his residence to Yongle Palace.
idiomatic: He moved his residence to Yongle Palace.

literal: Later, when the emperor held court in the Hall of Audience, he once told Liang: "The rites of the Three Dynasties had the sun rise for audience at court.
idiomatic: Later at the Hall of Audience the emperor told Liang, "The Three Dynasties held court as the sun rose."

literal: From Han and Wei downward, ceremony gradually decayed.
idiomatic: "From Han and Wei onward ceremony decayed."

literal: The Jin ordinance had on the first and fifteenth of the month the gathering of ministers at the Hall of Audience to discuss government, yet there was no text of the Son of Heaven attending in person.
idiomatic: "Jin ordinances gathered ministers on the first and fifteenth to discuss government, yet never required the Son of Heaven in person."

literal: Now because you gather at midday, before noon you yourselves shall discuss government;
idiomatic: "Now that you gather at midday, before noon you shall discuss government among yourselves;"

literal: after noon I shall deliberate with you what may or may not be done.
idiomatic: "after noon I shall deliberate with you what may or may not be done."

literal: Thereupon he ordered memorials read aloud and personally decided them.
idiomatic: He then had memorials read aloud and decided them himself.

literal: At the transfer of the capital he was made Grand General of Martial Guards and, in his existing office, supervised central military affairs.
idiomatic: At the capital transfer he was made Grand General of Martial Guards and, retaining his existing posts, oversaw central military affairs.

literal: When the emperor campaigned south, Liang was put in charge of Masters of Writing affairs and left to guard Luoyang.
idiomatic: On the southern campaign the emperor put Liang in charge of Masters of Writing affairs and left him to guard Luoyang.

literal: Later the emperor from Xiaoping Ford took a boat to Shiji.
idiomatic: Later the emperor took a boat from Xiaoping Ford to Shiji.

literal: Liang admonished: "The Han emperor wished to cross the Wei by boat; Guangde was about to stain the chariot wheels with blood from his head, and the emperor was moved and went to the bridge.
idiomatic: Liang admonished, "When a Han emperor wished to cross the Wei by boat, Guangde threatened to stain the chariot wheels with his own blood, and the emperor was moved to take the bridge instead."

literal: That small stream of the Wei was still like this—how much more the great river, with its immeasurable peril!
idiomatic: "That small stream of the Wei was still so perilous—how much more this great river, with dangers no man can measure!"

literal: The emperor said: "The Minister of Works speaks rightly.
idiomatic: The emperor said, "The Minister of Works is right."

literal: When Pi's involvement in Mu Tai's rebellion came to light, Liang submitted a memorial impeaching himself; the emperor issued a gracious edict and ordered him to resume his duties.
idiomatic: When Pi's involvement in Mu Tai's rebellion came to light, Liang memorialized to impeach himself; the emperor answered graciously and ordered him to resume his duties.

literal: Liang firmly refused; only after long delay was he permitted.
idiomatic: Liang firmly refused; only after long insistence was permission granted.

literal: Later his fief was changed to Duke of Dunqiu to continue the ennobled line.
idiomatic: His fief was later changed to Duke of Dunqiu to continue the ennobled line.

literal: When Emperor Xuanwu took the throne, Liang was appointed Director of the Masters of Writing and Minister of Works.
idiomatic: At Emperor Xuanwu's accession he was made Director of the Masters of Writing and Minister of Works.

literal: He died; Emperor Xuanwu personally attended the lesser obsequies, posthumously made him Grand Commandant, posthumous title Kuang.
idiomatic: He died; Emperor Xuanwu personally attended the lesser obsequies, posthumously made him Grand Commandant with the posthumous title Kuang.

literal: His son Shao, courtesy name Yongye, married the Princess of Langye and was appointed Commandant of the Horse Guards.
idiomatic: His son Shao, courtesy name Yongye, married the Princess of Langye and was made Commandant of the Horse Guards.

literal: He held in succession Director of the Secretariat, Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of the Guards, Minister of Ceremonies, Director of the Palace Secretariat, and the two Directors of the Seven Arms Hall.
idiomatic: He served in turn as Director of the Secretariat, Attendant-in-Ordinary, General of the Guards, Minister of Ceremonies, Director of the Palace Secretariat, and both Directors of the Seven Arms Hall.

literal: He met with mourning for his birth mother, was dismissed, and in residence for mourning was famed for filial piety.
idiomatic: When his birth mother died he left office; his mourning conduct won renown for filial piety.

literal: He again held Grand General of the Guards, Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Rectifier of his native commandery.
idiomatic: He later returned as Grand General of the Guards, Supervisor of the Palace Secretariat, Attendant-in-Ordinary, and Rectifier of his native commandery.

literal: Shao had no other talent, but his nature was square and weighty; he rarely received guests and seldom crossed others' thresholds.
idiomatic: Shao had no special talent, but his nature was square and grave; he rarely received guests and seldom crossed another man's threshold.

literal: The commander Yuan Cha, when power blazed, once went to Shao's residence; Shao merely met and escorted him down the steps.
idiomatic: When Commander Yuan Cha's power blazed, he once visited Shao's house; Shao merely met him at the gate and saw him down the steps.

literal: Men of the time admired and exalted this.
idiomatic: Contemporaries admired him for it.

literal: When the Empress Dowager Ling wished to depose Cha but hesitated and had not decided, Shao urged approval.
idiomatic: When Empress Dowager Ling wished to depose Cha but hesitated, Shao urged her to act.

literal: For this merit he was given special advancement and Attendant-in-Ordinary.
idiomatic: For this service he received special advancement and Attendant-in-Ordinary.

literal: Yuan Shun and Shao shared duty; once, drunk, he entered Shao's sleeping quarters.
idiomatic: Yuan Shun shared duty with Shao; once, drunk, he entered Shao's sleeping quarters.

literal: Shao threw off the quilt and rose, sternly reproaching Shun: "This old man has been Attendant-in-Ordinary twenty years and with your late father repeatedly held office together; though you are junior in rank, how may you crowd and affront me!
idiomatic: Shao threw off his quilt and rose, sternly reproaching him: "I have been Attendant-in-Ordinary twenty years and served repeatedly with your late father; though you are junior in rank, how dare you crowd and affront me!"

literal: He thereupon resigned and returned home; only after an edict admonished him did he rise.
idiomatic: He thereupon resigned and went home; only when an edict admonished him did he return to office.

literal: He was again made Attendant-in-Ordinary but pleaded illness and did not rise; therefore he escaped the calamity at Heyin.
idiomatic: He was again made Attendant-in-Ordinary but pleaded illness and did not take up the post, and so escaped the massacre at Heyin.

literal: When Emperor Zhuang was established, Erzhu Rong summoned him.
idiomatic: When Emperor Zhuang was enthroned, Erzhu Rong summoned him.

literal: Shao thought he would surely die and wept before the family shrine in farewell.
idiomatic: Shao believed he would surely die and wept farewell before the family shrine.

literal: When he met Rong he clasped his hands and did not bow.
idiomatic: Meeting Rong, he clasped his hands and did not bow.

literal: Rong also affected courtesy toward him and, turning to others, said: "Mu Shao does not falsely bear the name of a great house.
idiomatic: Rong likewise affected courtesy and said to those around him, "Mu Shao does not falsely bear the name of a great house."

literal: When the imperial carriage entered the palace, he was soon appointed Director of the Masters of Writing and Minister of Works, advanced to prince, given forty halberds of the imperial guard, and still made Attendant-in-Ordinary.
idiomatic: When the emperor entered the palace he was soon made Director of the Masters of Writing and Minister of Works, advanced to prince, granted forty halberds of the imperial guard, and retained Attendant-in-Ordinary.

literal: At that time the Governor of Henan, Li Jiang, went to call on Shao.
idiomatic: At that time Li Jiang, Governor of Henan, went to call on Shao.

literal: Jiang, as a fellow townsman of Shao, thought he would surely receive a bow.
idiomatic: Jiang, as Shao's fellow townsman, expected a bow in return.

literal: Shao also relied on his fief being Jiang's sovereign state and sat upright waiting for him, not bending his knees.
idiomatic: Shao also relied on his fief being Jiang's sovereign state and sat upright awaiting him without rising.

literal: Jiang feared his rank and standing, performed a bow and withdrew.
idiomatic: Jiang, fearing his rank and standing, bowed and withdrew.
